facts.raw_span: A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness
A 34-year-old woman
gravida 2 para 1
previous cesarean section
presented at 4 weeks 5 days of amenorrhea
1-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen
denied fever, nausea, vomiting, or vaginal bleeding
afebrile, hemodynamically stable
epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding
Murphy’s and McBurney’s signs were negative
white blood cell count of 13.54×10^9/L
β-hCG level of 523 IU/L
empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness

concepts.why: The patient presents with amenorrhea, epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, and a β-hCG level below the discriminatory zone, with an empty uterine cavity on ultrasound, which are all consistent with an ectopic pregnancy.
The patient's epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen and epigastric tenderness, combined with the presence of a left adnexal structure on ultrasound, could be indicative of ovarian torsion.
The patient's β-hCG level and empty uterine cavity on ultrasound, along with the presence of a left adnexal structure, could be consistent with a corpus luteum cyst.
The patient's epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, epigastric tenderness, and elevated white blood cell count could be indicative of pelvic inflammatory disease.
The patient's epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, epigastric tenderness, and presence of free fluid in the pouch of Douglas could be indicative of a ruptured ovarian cyst.

rationales.F04: Short duration of amenorrhea increases suspicion for ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F05: Epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen is a common symptom of ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion.
rationales.F08: Epigastric tenderness is a common finding in ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion.
rationales.F10: Elevated white blood cell count may indicate infection or inflammation, which can be seen in pelvic inflammatory disease.
rationales.F11: β-hCG level is below the discriminatory zone, increasing suspicion for ectopic pregnancy.
rationales.F12: Empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness on ultrasound is highly suggestive of ectopic pregnancy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with epigastric pain radiating to the lower abdomen, a β-hCG level of 523 IU/L, and an empty uterus with normal endometrial thickness on ultrasound, combined with the absence of vaginal bleeding and a short duration of amenorrhea, strongly supports the diagnosis of an ectopic pregnancy.
